area: Juniper Plains Area, Larkspur Valley (invented example community)
note: Invented drill fiction: the Juniper Plains Area, the Larkspur Valley, its towns, rivers, roads, dam and every organization and person are made up (simulation/example/world.json). Scenarios select units by geography and flags; organization names come from the organization pack at run time. A community's own real scenarios live beside its directory export (<export>/simulation/scenarios/), never in this repository. Independent volunteer project, not an official Church product.

scenarios.name: Copper Creek Dam failure, Larkspur Valley flood
scenarios.summary: 07:50 on Sunday 21 March, daylight, +4 °C and light rain after three days of warm rain on a deep snowpack. Copper Creek Dam seeps, then fails at T+38. The county orders Copper Ridge below the dam and the Copper Creek corridor through south Larkspur out and warns the river bottoms and Alder Flat; the Stake Presidents must decide about the 9:00 meetings. The flood wave takes the Route 30 bridge at Copper Ridge (T+45), surrounds the Larkspur Care Center and closes the Route 12 bridge (T+70), floods the substation and cuts the fibre (T+75 to T+78), crests through Larkspur West and reaches Alder Flat (T+140). Care-facility residents without transport, missionaries not accounted for, Spanish-speaking families, a dam rumour, unasked volunteers, Supply Orders, a storehouse truck by the long way round, city requests by ICS 213RR and a wet-snow night.
scenarios.pace: P (congested) for 80 minutes, then C when the south loses power and fibre; A at T+175 after a round-trip test; P for the north wards at T+225.
scenarios.severity: feature polygons: band 3 in the flood path of Copper Creek, band 2 in the Larkspur River flood plain or the evacuation-order zone, band 1 in the warning zone, 0 elsewhere (the north stakes host evacuees); care-facility and retirement branches at least 2, the Spanish-language branch at least 1
lessons: late or absent official alert: the stake notifies its own members, in Spanish too
Sunday meetings cancelled before members drive into the water
911 saturated: relay life-safety calls in writing
health-and-welfare traffic policy
unit not heard from
county liaison: one consolidated message per slot
verified versus reported missing (members with relatives)
care facility without transport, roll call at the destination
satellite terminal without operator, power or sky
repeater dies: relay plan, 72-hour posture
rumour verified before relay
Winlink congestion: traffic priority
false fulfilled and duplicate Supply Orders
public shelter, usage agreement, six shelter figures
unasked volunteers and goods
cold wet night, fuel and generators (carbon monoxide)

scenarios.name: Larkspur fault earthquake under the west bench, M 6.9
scenarios.summary: A winter weekday at 06:30 in the dark. The invented Larkspur fault ruptures along the foot of the west bench from Saddleback to Juniper Springs. Older brick homes and the Larkspur downtown fail; the Center Street bridge is closed for inspection, splitting Larkspur West from the county seat; the river bottoms liquefy around Alder Flat; Copper Creek Dam is inspected and holds. Power out valley-wide, cellular fails within minutes, the Saddleback Peak repeater is damaged.
scenarios.pace: P for 10 minutes, then C (VARA HF where the repeater is down); A at T+170 after a round-trip test; P late in the drill if at all.
scenarios.severity: distance bands 5 / 12 / 30 km from an epicentre under Saddleback; +1 in the river flood plain (liquefaction); care facilities at least band 2
lessons: repeater damaged: simplex and HF from the start
Satellite EOC behind a closed bridge
unreinforced masonry, injuries at the meetinghouse
gas leaks and carbon monoxide in the cold
missing list verified household by household

scenarios.name: Wind-driven wildland fire on Saddleback Ridge
scenarios.summary: A late-August afternoon fire starts on Saddleback Ridge and runs down the west bench on a dry wind. Saddleback and the Larkspur West bench neighbourhoods evacuate; Route 30 west closes for smoke; the Saddleback Peak repeater is threatened and goes off the air when its site burns. Shelters at the Juniper Springs stake center and the fairgrounds for horses and livestock; Supply Orders for cots, water and air filters.
scenarios.pace: P in the valley; C for the bench wards when their cell sites burn; the net moves to simplex when the repeater is lost.
scenarios.severity: band 3 inside the fire polygon on the west bench, band 2 within 2 km of it, band 1 for the rest of Saddleback and Larkspur West, 0 elsewhere
lessons: order without prior warning: zone, timestamp, action
the repeater site burns: relay plan
livestock and people without transport
false alert to the wrong area
unasked volunteers and donations

scenarios.name: January ice storm: valley-wide outage, five days of cold
scenarios.summary: Day 2 of an ice storm. Ice-loaded lines and trees have taken power from most of the valley; Route 12 is glare ice; temperatures fall to −18 °C at night. Welfare checks on the elderly, care facilities on generators, meetinghouses opened as warming centres, generator fuel and carbon monoxide.
scenarios.pace: P while cell sites hold battery; A from the stake center Starlink; C as sites go dark on day 2.
scenarios.severity: band 2 everywhere; band 3 for care facilities and for units outside the towns
lessons: heat, fuel and water per person on the Supply Order
72-hour posture and shift relief
people sleeping in cars at the shelter
carbon monoxide from generators indoors

scenarios.name: Downslope windstorm out of Copper Creek canyon, 110 km/h gusts
scenarios.summary: An east wind pours out of the Copper Creek canyon before dawn: trees and lines down across Copper Ridge and east Larkspur, roofs off, thousands without power. A short, common event for practising the normal paths and a scheduled slide to Alternate as cell sites lose backup power.
scenarios.pace: P, then A at T+60 as cell sites lose battery.
scenarios.severity: band 2 in Copper Ridge and east Larkspur, band 1 elsewhere in the Larkspur council, 0 in the Kestrel council
lessons: cell outage timeline: power first, then backhaul
chainsaw crews: team leaders and the safety acknowledgment

scenarios.name: Rail tank-car release at the Kestrel grain elevators, shelter in place
scenarios.summary: A derailment at the Kestrel grain elevators ruptures a tank car of anhydrous ammonia on a still morning. The county hazardous-materials team orders shelter in place for a 3 km downwind sector over Kestrel and the Pine Hollow farms. Nobody moves, so no runners and no crews: accountability by phone and radio only until the all-clear.
scenarios.pace: P throughout (an exercise in restraint, not in radio).
scenarios.severity: band 3 inside the plume sector polygon, band 1 within 5 km, 0 elsewhere
lessons: shelter in place versus evacuate: one written authority for the order
people without transport
members outside the zone stay home

scenarios.name: Spring snowmelt flood on the Larkspur River, without dam failure
scenarios.summary: A record snowpack melts in a warm week. Day 3 of high water: the Larkspur River is over its banks from Kestrel through Riverside to Alder Flat; Pine Hollow Creek floods farms above Kestrel. Sandbag crews, pumps, basements, evacuations of the bottoms, days of status reports.
scenarios.pace: P and A throughout; a Contingency slice for crews out of cell range in the bottoms.
scenarios.severity: band 3 inside the river flood plain polygon, band 2 within 1.5 km of it, otherwise 0 to 1
lessons: the stake notifies its own members when the official alert is late
missing list inflation then verification
volunteer gridlock: one hub, pre-registered teams
shelter lost to the water

scenarios.name: Regional power and telecom failure, 72 hours, cause unknown
scenarios.summary: No damage, no casualties, no power, no cellular, no internet anywhere in the valley for three days. Pure PACE discipline: radio only, then Starlink at the stake center; the coordinating council reached by Winlink HF.
scenarios.pace: C from T+0; A for the EOC's own internet from T+60 (Starlink); never P.
scenarios.severity: band 1 everywhere, band 2 for care facilities
lessons: cell sites die from power, then backhaul: batteries 4 to 8 hours
no scheduled step-up: plan for no communications for 72 hours

scenarios.name: Multi-vehicle crash with a youth bus on Route 12 in fog
scenarios.summary: A Saturday-morning pile-up on Route 12 north of Juniper Springs involves a bus taking youth to a stake activity. Not a Church emergency: the county leads. The Church's role is member accountability and support for families; it practises restraint, correct traffic and the Stake President's judgement about what goes up the line.
scenarios.severity: band 2 for the two units nearest the crash site and the youth's home units, 0 elsewhere
lessons: health-and-welfare inquiries flood the net
the hospital at capacity: families gather at the stake center

lessons_note: lessons: the failure modes from the 2024–2026 disaster research (docs/SIMULATOR_LESSONS.md) each scenario rehearses, or should when its outline is written out.
